planting.note: Direct sow from early spring through midsummer in deep, loose, stone-free soil in full sun; Berlicum can be sown successively for a summer-through-winter harvest.

directions: Direct sow into deep, loose, stone-free soil in full sun; Berlicum is a classic Dutch maincrop carrot producing smooth, blunt-tipped orange roots 7-9 inches long with a small core, maturing in about 80 days. It can be sown from February through August for a continuous summer-to-winter supply and stores well once pulled, making it a dependable workhorse for both fresh eating and juicing. Thin seedlings early to 2-3 inches apart for straight, well-formed roots.

planting.note: Direct sow into deep, loose, light or sandy soil in full sun; Long Red Surrey needs stone-free soil for its long tapering roots to form straight.

directions: Direct sow into deep, loose, light or sandy soil in full sun; Long Red Surrey is an English heirloom carrot dating to the 1830s, producing long, tapering orange roots with a yellow core, best grown in light, well-drained ground where its length can develop without forking. It matures in 75-85 days with a strong, sweet flavor that has kept it in cultivation as an exhibition and storage carrot for nearly two centuries. Thin seedlings early to allow full root development and harvest before hard freeze for the best texture.

planting.note: Direct sow into very deep, loose, stone-free soil in full sun; New Red Intermediate needs extra-deep cultivation for its long, pointed exhibition-length roots.

directions: Direct sow into very deep, loose, stone-free soil in full sun; New Red Intermediate is a classic English show and exhibition carrot with very long, pointed roots falling between half-long and long carrot types, part of the historical lineage behind record-length show carrots. Maturing in 80-100+ days, it produces sweet, tender flesh that keeps well into winter storage. Double-dig or use a deep raised bed to give the roots the uninterrupted depth they need to grow straight and reach full exhibition length.

planting.note: Direct sow into deep, loose, fertile soil in full sun; Rodelika was bred for high sugar content, making it a favorite for home juicing.

directions: Direct sow into deep, loose, fertile soil in full sun; Rodelika is a German biodynamic carrot bred at Dottenfelderhof and registered in 1998, producing long, blunt, deep orange-red roots prized for their unusually high sugar content. It matures in about 75-80 days and is a favorite among home growers for fresh juicing as well as general kitchen use, and it stores well through winter. Thin seedlings early to give roots room to reach full length and sweetness.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; transplant into fertile, moisture-retentive soil once frost danger has passed. Tellus is an old English heirloom valued for genuine, strong celeriac flavor.

directions: Transplant into fertile, consistently moist soil in full sun; Tellus is an old English heirloom celeriac sourced from the UK's Heritage Seed Library, producing vigorous roots slightly darker than modern hybrid types with distinctive reddish leaf stalks. It matures in roughly 110 days and is cold-hardy to around 25°F, allowing late-season harvest after light frost. Growers favor it for its genuinely strong, old-fashioned celeriac flavor, which many modern bred-for-smoothness cultivars have lost; keep soil evenly moist throughout the season to avoid hollow or cracked roots.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant into fertile, well-drained soil for a late summer or fall harvest.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Famosa is a Bejo-bred hybrid savoy cabbage with dark-green, heavily savoyed leaves wrapping bright green, compact round heads of 2-4 pounds. It matures in about 70 days from transplant and shows good disease tolerance along with the mild, tender flavor savoy types are known for. Spring-sow for a late summer or fall harvest, and expect it to hold well in the garden without splitting for a reasonable harvest window.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; transplant in late spring for a fall harvest. Lodero carries clubroot resistance, a genuine advantage in soil with a history of that disease.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Lodero is a Bejo-bred red cabbage notable as the first clubroot-resistant red cabbage cultivar, a significant advantage in gardens with a history of that soilborne disease. Medium heads of 3-6 pounds are held high off the ground, maturing in roughly 105 days from a late-April-to-May sowing for a late September to November harvest. It stores exceptionally well into winter and makes excellent pickled red cabbage or braised dishes.

planting.note: Start seed indoors a few weeks before last frost; transplant for a long-season harvest meant for winter storage rather than fresh summer eating.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Langedijker is a centuries-old Dutch heirloom cabbage named for the Langedijk region, producing large, firm, round heads of about 4 pounds that hold their light color exceptionally well in long-term storage. It needs a long season, 120-150 days, to reach full size and density, making it best suited to an early spring start and a fall harvest timed just before hard freeze. This is the classic winter-keeper and sauerkraut cabbage of Dutch tradition, bred specifically for root-cellar storage rather than immediate fresh use.

planting.note: Direct sow in early spring or late summer for a fall crop into fertile, well-drained soil; Sorrento matures very fast and bolts quickly in heat, so avoid summer sowings.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Sorrento is a fast-maturing Italian broccoli raab producing uniform, dark green florets about 2 inches across on blue-green plants, ready in just 40 days from seed. Sow in late summer for a fall harvest or very early spring for a spring crop, since hot weather pushes it to bolt quickly. Harvest the whole flowering shoot while buds are still tight and sauté with garlic and olive oil, the classic preparation for this slightly bitter, mineral-rich green.

planting.note: Direct sow into deep, loose, stone-free soil in full sun; parsnip seed is slow and sometimes erratic to germinate, so keep the bed consistently moist until seedlings emerge.

directions: Direct sow into deep, loose, stone-free soil in full sun; Melbourne Whiteskin is an old Australian heirloom parsnip with long, smooth, tapered white roots carrying a sweet, nutty flavor that improves further after a frost. It is a vigorous grower with good tolerance of common parsnip pests and diseases, maturing in about 120 days. Leave roots in the ground through the first hard frosts of fall to maximize sweetness, then harvest as needed for roasting, steaming, or adding to soups and stews.
